claim:
For every \(0<w<1\), equip the real vector plane with the Lorentz-predual norm
\[
N_w(s,t)=\max\left\{|s|,|t|,\frac{|s|+|t|}{1+w}\right\}.
\]
For every nonempty bounded set \(S\) let \(r_w(S)=\inf_{c\in\mathbb R^2}\sup_{x\in S}N_w(x-c)\) and \(d_w(S)=\sup_{x,y\in S}N_w(x-y)\). Its Jung constant, with radius-to-diameter normalization \(J(X_w)=\sup_{d_w(S)>0}2r_w(S)/d_w(S)\), is exactly
\[
J(X_w)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{3(1+w)}{3+w},&0<w\le\dfrac13,\\[2mm]
\dfrac4{3+w},&\dfrac13\le w\le\sqrt2-1,\\[2mm]
\dfrac{2(1+w)}{2+w},&\sqrt2-1\le w\le\dfrac12,\\[2mm]
\dfrac3{2+w},&\dfrac12\le w<1.
\end{cases}
\]
Consequently, the maximum of \(J(X_w)\) throughout this family is \(6/5\), attained at exactly two parameters \(w=1/3\) and \(w=1/2\). At the intermediate regular-octagon parameter \(w=\sqrt2-1\), the profile has a strict local minimum with \(J(X_w)=4-2\sqrt2\). Every branch is witnessed by an explicit three-point set of diameter one, and all upper bounds hold for arbitrary bounded sets, not only triangles.

correctness.rationale: For the norm represented by eight signed coordinate/diagonal forms, linear-programming duality expresses every Chebyshev radius as a maximum over balanced probability measures on these forms. Three affine constraints restrict extreme measures to opposite pairs or minimal triples. Up to the full coordinate symmetry, every triple has one of two relations: \(f_1+f_2=k f_3\) or \(2f_1=k(f_3+f_4)\). Three explicit facet inequalities give the Type I numerator at most \(\min\{2,3k/2\}\), and two independent inequalities give the Type II numerator at most \(\min\{2k,3\}\). Every bound is attained on an explicit diameter-one triple, including all interval endpoints. Pair circuits yield no larger value. Comparing the two sharp rational functions proves the four branches and all stated extrema, without any finite-enumeration inference.
risks: The theorem is real and two-dimensional; it makes no assertion for infinite-dimensional or complex Lorentz spaces.
A numerical LP check of sample parameters is only a cross-check; all parameter quantifiers are established by the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The Jung constant is a natural intrinsic covering invariant, the sharp smallest enclosing-ball radius relative to diameter. The weighted Lorentz-predual octagons form a classical continuous Banach-plane family interpolating between the square and a rotated square and containing the regular octagon. Its exact Jung constant was previously available only at isolated special shapes in the checked literature. The complete phase diagram reveals two genuinely distinct off-regular worst shapes with equal value 6/5 and a regular-octagon local trough: this nonmonotone shape dependence is structural information relevant to Chebyshev centers, equilateral configurations, and comparisons of normed-plane geometric constants. The result also supplies explicit sharp witness triples and universal diameter-one upper bounds rather than numerical approximations.
risks: The result is a complete classification of one natural one-parameter family, not a formula for arbitrary centrally symmetric octagons.
The universal definition and finite-dimensional duality are classical; the family-specific sharp parameter stratification and two peaks supply the nonroutine value.
